group.passage: Ask your grandparents what they ate for breakfast as children, and many will say congee, a soft rice porridge often made from rice left over from dinner. Ask your classmates, and you may hear about sandwiches from a breakfast shop. This small change at the breakfast table is part of a much bigger story: people in Taiwan are eating less rice than before. The chart below shows how much rice and wheat there was for each person in Taiwan to eat every day from 1985 to 2025. In 1985, there were about 220 grams of rice for each person a day, but only 68 grams of wheat. By 2025, rice had dropped to 114 grams, about half of what it had been. Wheat, which is used to make bread and noodles, went the other way. It rose to 106 grams in 2005 and has moved up and down a little since then. How did this happen? Part of the answer goes back to the 1950s, when the United States gave wheat and flour to Taiwan. In the 1960s, a campaign encouraged people to eat more wheat foods, and some newspapers even claimed that Westerners were taller because they ate bread. Later, quick breakfast stands made sandwiches as common in the morning as steamed buns. Daily life has changed, too. The government's farm agency points out that Western-style meals and eating out have changed the way people eat rice, and young people prefer noodles and baked goods. In 2022, people in Taiwan ate more meat than grains for the first time since records began. Eating less rice is bad news for rice farmers. To help them, the government now encourages food makers to grind rice into flour and mix it with wheat flour in bread and noodles. Perhaps the next sandwich you buy will have a little rice inside.

translation_zh.text:
問問你的祖父母小時候早餐吃什麼，很多人會說稀飯，一種常用前一天晚餐剩下的米飯煮成的軟粥。問問你的同學，你可能會聽到早餐店的三明治。早餐桌上的這個小改變，是一個更大故事的一部分：台灣人吃的米比以前少了。
下面的圖表顯示 1985 到 2025 年，台灣每人每天有多少米和小麥可以吃。1985 年，每人每天大約有 220 公克的米，小麥卻只有 68 公克。到了 2025 年，米已經降到 114 公克，大約只剩原來的一半。用來做麵包和麵條的小麥則走向相反的方向：它在 2005 年升到 106 公克，之後就小幅上下變動。
這是怎麼發生的？部分原因可以追溯到 1950 年代，當時美國把小麥和麵粉送給台灣。1960 年代，有一項活動鼓勵大家多吃麵食，有些報紙甚至宣稱西方人比較高是因為吃麵包。後來，快速的早餐攤讓三明治在早上變得和饅頭一樣常見。
日常生活也改變了。政府的農業機關指出，西式飲食和外食改變了大家吃米的方式，而年輕人比較喜歡麵食和烘焙食品。2022 年，台灣人吃的肉類首次超過穀類，這是有紀錄以來的第一次。
吃米變少對米農是壞消息。為了幫助他們，政府現在鼓勵食品業者把米磨成粉，和麵粉混合做成麵包和麵條。也許你下一次買的三明治裡，就有一點點米。
